name: Identity Chain: Kerberoast TGS request (RC4 against SPN account)
description: Win event 4769 with ticket encryption type 0x17 (RC4-HMAC) for a non-machine target. Catches id-01-kerberoast — TGS pulled for svc-deploy by an unprivileged member-machine session. RC4 is the smoking gun because modern Windows defaults to AES; only crackable RC4 tickets are usually attacker-driven.
query: event.code : "4769" and winlog.event_data.TicketEncryptionType : "0x17" and not winlog.event_data.ServiceName : (*$ or krbtgt)
author: Hunt Lab

name: Identity Chain: PowerShell Kerberoasting via KerberosRequestorSecurityToken
description: PowerShell command line referencing System.IdentityModel.Tokens.KerberosRequestorSecurityToken — the .NET class used by the Atomic T1558.003 Test 2 PowerShell-only kerberoaster. Higher-fidelity than the 4769-only signal because it catches the offensive tooling on the source host.
query: event.dataset : "windows.sysmon_operational" and event.code : "1" and process.name : ("powershell.exe" or "pwsh.exe") and process.command_line : *KerberosRequestorSecurityToken*
author: Hunt Lab

name: Identity Chain: Mimikatz lsadump::dcsync command line
description: Process command line containing 'lsadump::dcsync' — the canonical DCSync invocation. Catches id-02-dcsync via the Atomic T1003.006 mimikatz launch even when run on the DC where 4662-based detections are noisier.
author: Hunt Lab

name: Identity Chain: Directory Service replication GUIDs accessed (4662)
description: Win event 4662 with Properties referencing DS-Replication-Get-Changes (1131f6aa-9c07-11d1-f79f-00c04fc2dcd2) or DS-Replication-Get-Changes-All (1131f6ad-9c07-11d1-f79f-00c04fc2dcd2). Production rules suppress the DC computer accounts; in this lab we want the noise so the demo shows the underlying primitive.
author: Hunt Lab

name: Identity Chain: Mimikatz kerberos::golden command line
description: Process command line containing 'kerberos::golden' — Mimikatz golden-ticket forge. Catches id-03-golden-ticket. In a real intrusion this fires hours-to-days after a DCSync; pairing this rule with rule 03/04 in the same host within 48h is a high-confidence golden-ticket chain detection.
author: Hunt Lab

name: Identity Chain: Mimikatz kerberos::ptt (Pass the Ticket)
description: Process command line containing 'kerberos::ptt' — Mimikatz ticket import. Pairs with rule 05 to confirm the forged ticket was actually used (id-04-pass-the-ticket).
author: Hunt Lab

name: Identity Chain: setspn -A registration (SPN added)
description: setspn.exe invoked with -A or -S to register a Service Principal Name. Catches id-00-prep-spn and any subsequent attacker-driven SPN registration intended to make an account kerberoastable. Low severity because this also fires on legitimate provisioning — useful as a hunt pivot, not a high-priority alert.
query: event.dataset : "windows.sysmon_operational" and event.code : "1" and process.name : "setspn.exe" and process.args : ("-A" or "-S")
author: Hunt Lab

name: Identity Chain: DCSync followed by golden-ticket forge on same host
description: Sequence detection — Mimikatz DCSync followed within 6 hours by a golden-ticket forge anywhere in the lab. Highest-confidence identity-attack chain alert: by itself either rule has false positives, but the pair within a short window is essentially diagnostic.
query:
sequence with maxspan=6h
  [process where event.code == "1" and process.command_line like "*lsadump::dcsync*"]
  [process where event.code == "1" and process.command_line like "*kerberos::golden*"]
author: Hunt Lab
